problem_type: Planner host messages omit an existing shared screen-visibility constraint
symptom: First planning and revision requests do not contain the established screen-visibility rule, failing the two unchanged original storyboard regressions.
direct_cause: buildStoryboardPlanningMessage builds both host envelopes without referencing SCREEN_VISIBILITY_PROMPT_RULE, though the shared shot compiler owner already exports it.
class_root: Every planning mode and revision must receive the shared physical screen-visibility invariant at the host envelope boundary, without rewriting user story/plan data or copying another policy body.
affected_population: Revisions of existing plans with selected models, prompts and user parameters
entry_points: Existing downstream shot prompt compiler -> SCREEN_VISIBILITY_PROMPT_RULE
internal_only_reason: The rule is an existing internal physical-framing policy with a shared compiler owner and explicit failing tests. No provider behavior, model, billing or external framework changes are assumed.
invariants: Reference the existing exported rule once in each host envelope; do not duplicate its policy body
Keep story trimming and revision JSON/request serialization exactly as before
Do not mutate input, model keys, plan prompts, user parameters or canonical saved data
Do not change final shot compiler, routing, privileges, billing, cancellation or retries

door_reduction.why_not: Keep the existing compiler consumer and planner runner as separate legitimate lifecycles. The new host-formatter read is the previously missing policy connection, not another policy owner or business workflow.

generality_proof: Six new actual-function cases cover all three shot modes for initial planning and revision. Each asserts exactly one full shared rule in the host section, outside delimiters, while exact story/current-plan JSON/revision text and frozen original input stay unchanged. Two original failing assertions and existing title-language tests remain intact.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Host envelope for both initial planning and revision references the shared invariant

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The real launcher consumes this host-message constructor for both fresh and revision inputs.
Existing compiler already consumes the same rule and avoids adding it again when its heading is present; no compiler body change or parallel rule is needed.

recurrence.reason: Any initial mode or revision can otherwise plan physically impossible visible screen contents before shot compilation.
same_class_scan: Generated actual buildStoryboardPlanningMessage and SCREEN_VISIBILITY_PROMPT_RULE doors across src/electron
Read both planner envelope branches and their runStoryboardPlanner caller
Read the shared constant and existing conditional screenVisibilityPromptRule compiler consumer
Read renderer barrel re-export; preserve the sole shared policy owner

prevention.invariant: Every fresh/revision planner envelope includes the existing shared visibility rule outside user data.
prevention.failure_mode: Regression rejects missing/repeated host rule or any alteration of exact story/plan/request boundaries.
prevention.strategy: Import the existing rule via the renderer barrel and reference it in the two existing branches, without another policy or migration.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove rule-free host-envelope behavior; keep all input/output APIs and original planning functionality.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuse the existing shared string export and pure host formatter; no library/runtime dependency changes.

migration: None; inputs and persisted prompts remain unchanged. Only future host planning envelopes gain the pre-existing constraint.
residual_risks: No Provider-generated storyboard or final rendered shot is verified; real visual/physical compliance remains coordination acceptance
No App, media or PNG baseline run
